attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No Yang-Mills estimate yet proves that mixed reflected Wilson hairpin quotients are nonzero, multiplicative, and Hadamard-semigroup in collar thickness.
steps: Fixed-collar reflection positivity and RG convergence give N^{(r)}\ge0 for every finite reflected Wilson block; this is the already valid closed-cone step.
The boundary OPE ansatz writes the collar-limit matrix as N^{(r)}=B^{(r)}\circ M^{(r)}. After diagonal normalization, M^{(r)}\ge0 is equivalent to q_r=Nh/Bh\ge0.
If q_r is a continuous Hadamard semigroup, then q_r=exp_circ(-rK). Differentiating z^*q_r z at r=0 on zero-sum vectors yields the CND sign for K.
Schoenberg's theorem gives the converse: CND K makes every q_r PSD, hence the same-theory OS form is positive after undoing only a diagonal congruence.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The exact finite q>=0 condition is valid, but the semigroup/log reduction and the boundary factorization N=B∘M remain analytic OPE assumptions for the locked Wilson algebra.

assumptions: For the chosen finite Wilson family, diagonal entries of N^{(r)} and B^{(r)} are positive and all B^{(r)}_{ij} used in the quotient are nonzero.
Additive reflected boundary contacts vanish or have already been absorbed by valid diagonal trace continuity; the remaining anomaly is multiplicative.
The normalized quotients q_r are Hermitian, continuous in r, satisfy q_0=1, and, for the log test, q_{r+s}=q_r\circ q_s.
RG convergence is valid for every reflected mixed Wilson matrix entry in the finite block, not merely for separated single loops.
definitions: source object: fixed-collar reflected Wilson OS matrices N^{(r)} obtained as RG limits, plus boundary Gram factors B^{(r)} from the mixed hairpin OPE.
target object: continuum OS matrix M^{(r)} on the same locked Wilson observables at the reflection plane, with no boundary-added algebra.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions through finite Schur preimages after collar collapse.
same-theory condition: N^{(r)}=B^{(r)}\circ M^{(r)} with B only a trace anomaly of the original Wilson observables; no new counterterm, quotient, or loop renormalization.

equations.label: Schur preimage obstruction
equations.latex: M^{(r)}=N^{(r)}\oslash B^{(r)},\qquad M^{(r)}\ge0\Longleftrightarrow q_r:=\widehat N^{(r)}\oslash\widehat B^{(r)}\ge0
equations.valid_when: B has nonzero entries and positive diagonal; hats denote diagonal normalization, so the equivalence is by positive diagonal congruence.

equations.label: Hadamard semigroup generator
equations.latex: q_{r+s}=q_r\circ q_s,\qquad q_r=\exp_{\circ}(-rK),\qquad \sum_{i,j}\bar z_i z_jK_{ij}\le0\ \ (\sum_i z_i=0)
equations.valid_when: q_r is a continuous nonvanishing Hermitian Hadamard semigroup; the last condition is the CND criterion for q_r\ge0 for all r.

equations.label: finite falsifier test
equations.latex: \det q_I<0\quad\text{or}\quad \exists z,\ \sum z_i=0,\ \sum_{i,j}\bar z_i z_jK_{ij}>0\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{OS bridge fails}
equations.valid_when: The determinant test is valid for any realized finite block; the log-quadratic falsifier is valid only under the semigroup hypothesis.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A realized Wilson triple with det(Nh/Bh)<0 is a direct falsifier. If semigroup is claimed, a zero-sum vector with positive K-quadratic invalidates the log certificate.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This bridge isolates the exact post-collar invariant: finite PSD of the normalized Schur preimage. The semigroup hypothesis upgrades many minor checks to one generator estimate.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a finite locked Wilson block, same-theory OS passage after collar removal is equivalent to PSD of q=Nh/Bh. If collar quotients form a continuous Hadamard semigroup, this is certified for all collar scales exactly by a CND logarithmic generator.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if mixed Wilson collar OPE cannot be expressed in the same locked algebra or if B has zeros/discontinuous phases generically.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if boundary OPE proves N=B∘M with q_r PSD for all finite Wilson blocks, or proves a valid Hadamard semigroup with CND generator.
control_decision.reason: The branch now has a compact finite-matrix bridge and a sharper analytic gap: prove Wilson boundary factorization/semigroup or compute a determinant falsifier.

dependency_updates.description: The formal collar passage remains valid; the post-collar step is now the finite PSD test q=Nh/Bh, not generic cone closedness.
The locked Wilson algebra must realize enough finite blocks to test Schur preimages; changing loop renormalization would change the theory.
Topology must control mixed reflected Wilson OPE entries and any collar-thickness semigroup, not just separated probes.

falsifiers: falsifier: a locked three-hairpin Wilson family with det(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B)<0 despite N\ge0 from fixed-collar reflection positivity.
falsifier: q_{r+s}\ne q_r\circ q_s because cusp or shared-footprint interactions depend on the order of collar collapse, making the log-CND certificate invalid.
falsifier: a zero or discontinuous phase in B_{ij} while N_{ij}\ne0, so the same-theory Schur preimage is not defined in the cutoff-removal topology.
falsifier: an indefinite additive boundary contact survives in mixed OS entries, showing that the multiplicative boundary Gram model omitted a valid obstruction.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 210 makes log-CND a conditional tool, not a theorem. The exact valid obstruction is finite positivity of q=Nh/Bh. Infinite-divisibility or Hadamard semigroup structure is the extra assumption that turns q>=0 into a generator test; without it, determinants are the real falsifier search.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the reflected Wilson hairpin OPE for three shared-footprint loops at two collar thicknesses; test q_{r+s}=q_r∘q_s and det(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B)>=0.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
